symbols.name: K

symbols.name: K'

symbols.name: r
symbols.role: Known transition rewards, including any discounting.

symbols.name: m_t
symbols.role: Stagewise lower shift used by the nonnegative compiler input.

symbols.name: M_t
symbols.role: Stagewise upper shift used by the nonnegative compiler input.

symbols.name: R

symbols.name: h_t^{+}
symbols.role: Normalized positive reward leaf.

symbols.name: h_t^{-}
symbols.role: Normalized complementary reward leaf.

symbols.name: \underline G
symbols.role: Derived lower bound on every complete return from the stagewise reward minima.

symbols.name: \overline G
symbols.role: Derived upper bound on every complete return from the stagewise reward maxima.

symbols.name: D
symbols.role: Derived width of the complete-return range.

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.role: Fixed ambient factual policy, implemented by the external response-function coins \(V_t\), and used off the factual state by retained-action interventions; it is never an optimized model component.

symbols.name: \pi_{\mathrm{base}}
symbols.role: Fixed ambient baseline policy used by switched coalition times and implemented through the external coalition response-function coins; it is never an optimized model component.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.role: Fixed positive-probability factual conditioning trajectory in the ambient model stratum.

symbols.name: x_t
symbols.role: Observed transition row at time \(t\).

symbols.name: y_t
symbols.role: Observed next state at time \(t\).

symbols.name: p_t
symbols.role: Local evidence probability used in posterior response-row constraints.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.role: Lower bound on factual transition-cell probabilities for uniform stability.

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M\) has the transition equations \(S_{t+1}=F_t(S_t,A_t,U_t)\), fixed initial state, and the fixed ambient externally randomized factual and coalition policies specified in \(\texttt{def:compatible-scm-class}\).
symbols.role: Candidate transition-response SCM under fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\); the policies are external mechanisms, not optimized components.

symbols.name: U_t
symbols.role: Time-\(t\) transition disturbance.

symbols.name: F_t
symbols.role: Time-\(t\) transition mechanism.

symbols.name: R_t
symbols.role: Joint potential-next-state table at time \(t\).

symbols.name: \lambda_t
symbols.role: Within-time response-table coupling.

symbols.name: \mathfrak M(K)
symbols.type: class of compatible Markov structural causal models
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M(K)\) abbreviates \(\mathfrak M(K;\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\), the class in \(\texttt{def:compatible-scm-class}\) for fixed ambient policies and trajectory.
symbols.role: Compatible transition-response SCM class; the fixed ambient policies are external and only the transition-response coupling varies.

symbols.name: \alpha_t^0
symbols.def: \(\alpha_t^0(\cdot\mid s_t)=\delta_{a_t}\) and \(\alpha_t^0(\cdot\mid s)=\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)\) for \(s\ne s_t\).
symbols.role: Retained-action intervention at time \(t\).

symbols.name: \alpha_t^1
symbols.role: Baseline-switch intervention at time \(t\).

symbols.name: \alpha^C
symbols.role: Fixed coalition policy induced by the ambient factual and baseline policies and sampled by the external coins \(V_t^C\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.role: Conditional transition kernel after abduction on \(\tau\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B(K,\tau)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)=\{q:q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t},\ q_{t,x}\in\Delta(\mathcal S),\ p_tq_{t,x}(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)\ \text{for all }t,x\ne x_t,y\}\).
symbols.role: Exact posterior row fiber.

symbols.name: g_C(q)
symbols.role: Counterfactual expected return for coalition \(C\).

symbols.name: \omega_H(C)
symbols.role: Shapley coalition weight.

symbols.name: \Phi_i(q)
symbols.role: Trajectory-conditioned Shapley mean-credit coordinate under posterior kernel \(q\).

symbols.name: \Theta_i(K,\tau)
symbols.def: \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(\mathcal M\mid\tau):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K)\}\) for fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\).
symbols.role: Transition-SCM identified set for the fixed ambient factual trajectory and external policies.

symbols.name: L_i(K,\tau)
symbols.role: Lower shared-SCM endpoint.  The displayed notation suppresses the fixed ambient policies \(\pi\) and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\).

symbols.name: U_i(K,\tau)
symbols.role: Upper shared-SCM endpoint.  The displayed notation suppresses the fixed ambient policies \(\pi\) and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\).

symbols.name: G_i^b(z,q)
symbols.def: \(G_i^b(z,q)\) is the Markov expected return with time \(i\) fixed to \(\alpha_i^b\) and every \(t\ne i\) independently mixed as \((1-z)\alpha_t^0+z\alpha_t^1\), for \(b\in\{0,1\}\).
symbols.role: Forced-membership branch of the Bernoulli-coalition representation.

symbols.name: P_i(z,q)
symbols.def: \(P_i(z,q)=G_i^0(z,q)-G_i^1(z,q)\), where \(G_i^b(z,q)\) is the Markov expected return with time \(i\) fixed to \(\alpha_i^b\) and each \(t\ne i\) independently mixed as \((1-z)\alpha_t^0+z\alpha_t^1\).
symbols.role: Bernoulli-coalition marginal-contribution polynomial.

symbols.name: \zeta_j
symbols.role: Interpolation nodes for exact Shapley integration.

symbols.name: \ell_j(z)
symbols.role: Interpolation basis associated with the rational quadrature nodes.

symbols.name: \nu_j
symbols.def: \(\nu_j=\int_0^1\ell_j(z)\,dz\), where \(\ell_j\) is the Lagrange basis polynomial for \(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_H\).
symbols.role: Exact integration weights for degree at most \(H-1\).

symbols.name: \mathsf Q_i(q)
symbols.role: Polynomial-size exact representation of the Shapley coordinate.

symbols.name: \sigma
symbols.role: Selects the upper or lower affine endpoint objective.

symbols.name: h_{jb}(q)
symbols.role: A branch expectation in \(\left[0,1\right]\) realized from normalized local reward leaves.

symbols.name: a_{jb}^{\sigma}
symbols.role: Signed coefficient in the affine nonnegative lift.

symbols.name: C_{\nu}
symbols.role: Quadrature offset; this is the constant denoted \(C\) in the affine recovery identity.

symbols.name: F_i^{\sigma}(q)
symbols.role: Concrete nonnegative objective for sign \(\sigma\), with the same posterior kernel \(q\) in every term.

symbols.name: V_{\sigma}
symbols.role: Maximized nonnegative objective from which a shared endpoint is recovered.

symbols.name: Z_{t,x}
symbols.def: \(Z_{t,x}\) selects one vertex of the row polytope for \((t,x)\).
symbols.role: Shared endpoint-optimization choice for one posterior row; singleton choices are substituted before the sparse-width order is run.

symbols.name: \mathfrak F_i^{\sigma}
symbols.def: For fixed \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), \(\mathfrak F_i^{\sigma}\) is the explicit circuit for \(F_i^{\sigma}\), using quadrature, forced-membership, path, and reward-time selectors, local leaves \(h_t^{+}\) and \(h_t^{-}\), and one shared copy of every \(Z_{t,x}\) across all selectors and paths.
symbols.role: Explicit polynomial-size nonnegative input whose legal mixed elimination returns the exact fixed-sign shared endpoint objective.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: \(N\) is the maximum number of variables plus factors in either explicit circuit \(\mathfrak F_i^{+1}\) or \(\mathfrak F_i^{-1}\).
symbols.role: Compiler input-size count.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d\) is the largest alphabet size of a nonglobal chance or decision variable in \(\mathfrak F_i^{+1}\) or \(\mathfrak F_i^{-1}\).
symbols.role: Compiler alphabet bound.

symbols.name: \mathsf{BP}_{\sigma}
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{BP}_{\sigma}\) records, at every maximization bucket of \(\mathfrak F_i^{\sigma}\), an optimizing value consistent with the already fixed outer decision context.
symbols.role: Backtracking data that recovers one joint assignment of all shared row selectors and hence one compatible endpoint SCM.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.role: Baseline-switch probability in the strict-gap family.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: For the binary two-stage strict-gap calculation, \(u=q_{1,(0,1)}(1)\).
symbols.role: Time-one alternate-action success probability.

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: For the binary two-stage strict-gap calculation, \(w=q_{2,(0,1)}(1)\).
symbols.role: Time-two baseline-action success probability at state zero.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: For the binary two-stage strict-gap calculation, \(z=q_{2,(1,0)}(1)\).
symbols.role: Time-two factual-policy success probability at state one.

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: For the binary two-stage strict-gap calculation, \(v=q_{2,(1,1)}(1)\).
symbols.role: Time-two baseline-action success probability at state one.

symbols.name: \mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}
symbols.type: one-parameter family of finite Markov SCM instances
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) is the explicit two-step binary family defined in \(\texttt{def:strict-gap-family}\).
symbols.role: Nondegenerate family separating shared and coalitionwise endpoint optimization.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)\) is obtained by minimizing or maximizing every distinct coalition return \(g_C\) over its own copy of \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) before forming the signed Shapley sum.
symbols.role: Independently optimized coalitionwise outer bound.

symbols.name: n_{t,x}
symbols.def: \(n_{t,x}\) is the fixed number of transition observations from row \((t,x)\).
symbols.role: Multinomial row sample sizes.

symbols.name: \widehat K
symbols.def: \(\widehat K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) is the empirical multinomial proportion vector from the \(n_{t,x}\) observations.
symbols.role: Estimated transition marginals.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.role: Familywise error probability.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)
symbols.role: Explicit simplex-intersected coordinate-box region calibrated by a cellwise Hoeffding union bound.

symbols.name: L_i^{\alpha}
symbols.role: Lower confidence-fiber endpoint.

symbols.name: U_i^{\alpha}
symbols.role: Upper confidence-fiber endpoint.

symbols.name: \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\) abbreviates the fixed-ambient subclass whose transition-response coordinates are mutually independent at every time, as defined in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-independent-subclass}\).
symbols.role: Transition-component product-response subclass; the superscript makes no assertion about an external full SCM scheme.

symbols.name: q^{\mathrm{CI}}
symbols.def: \(q_{t,x_t}^{\mathrm{CI}}=\delta_{y_t}\) and \(q_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(x\ne x_t\), at every \(t\in[H]\).
symbols.role: Unique transition posterior kernel selected by mutual independence of within-time transition-response coordinates.

symbols.name: \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)
symbols.def: \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(\mathcal M\mid\tau):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\}\) for fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\).
symbols.role: Identified transition-component mean-credit set after imposing mutual independence of the present model's transition-response coordinates.

symbols.name: \delta(K,K')
symbols.role: Uniform rowwise transition perturbation.

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: \(\theta=(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}})\) on the fixed two-stage binary stratum.
symbols.role: Joint transition, reward, factual-policy, and baseline-policy primitive.

symbols.name: \theta^\star
symbols.role: Interior center of the quantitative strict-gap family.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.role: Primitive-metric radius of the quantitative gap neighborhood.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm{pr}}
symbols.def: \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}\) is the maximum rowwise \(\ell^1\) discrepancy for transition and policy kernels and the sup discrepancy for reward cells, as specified in \(\texttt{def:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\).
symbols.role: Metric controlling simultaneous perturbations of \(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)=\{\theta:d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)<\rho\}\) within the valid fixed discrete stratum.
symbols.role: Certified open neighborhood on which the strict gap and nondegeneracy bounds hold.

symbols.name: \mu_\tau(\theta)
symbols.role: Observed probability mass of the fixed factual action-transition region.

symbols.name: s_\pi(\theta)
symbols.role: Smallest action probability across both policies.

symbols.name: s_K(\theta)
symbols.role: Smallest transition probability in the two-stage binary primitive.

symbols.name: V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)
symbols.role: Smallest conditional variance of the terminal reward across time-two rows.

symbols.name: \Delta_1^-(\theta)
symbols.role: Lower excess width of the internal coalitionwise relaxation over the shared-SCM interval.

symbols.name: \Delta_1^+(\theta)
symbols.role: Upper excess width of the internal coalitionwise relaxation over the shared-SCM interval.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W\) jointly indexes a quadrature node, a forced-membership branch, and a reward time in one endpoint circuit.
symbols.role: Single global selector whose alphabet contributes the leading \(2H^2\) factor but is excluded from constrained width.

symbols.name: \preceq
symbols.def: For either circuit \(\mathfrak F_i^{\sigma}\), \(\preceq\) is legal when every chance variable whose current factor scope contains an uneliminated decision variable is summed before that decision variable is maximized; the global sign is fixed, not eliminated.
symbols.role: Order preserving the outer shared-SCM maximization; the certified sparse order eliminates the path, then \(W\), then the active row selectors.

symbols.name: J
symbols.role: Stages at which factual conditioning does not force every posterior transition row to be a singleton.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: After singleton substitution, \(m\) is the number of remaining non-singleton posterior-row selectors specified by \(\texttt{def:active-ambiguity-count}\).
symbols.role: Active decision count controlling the certified sparse-stochastic constrained-width upper bound.

symbols.name: w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)
symbols.def: \(w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)\) is the maximum, over buckets induced by a legal order on either \(\mathfrak F_i^{\sigma}\), of the number of nonglobal live variables in the bucket minus one.
symbols.role: Constrained elimination width: at most \(m+3\) for the sparse order, but at least \(|J|-1\) on a fully active chain minor.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Compile}_i
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Compile}_i\) is the handle that applies legal sum-before-max elimination and \(\mathsf{BP}_{\sigma}\)-backtracking separately to the two fixed-sign circuits \(\mathfrak F_i^{+1}\) and \(\mathfrak F_i^{-1}\), without duplicating any \(Z_{t,x}\) within a circuit.
symbols.role: Exact rational compiler for both shared-SCM endpoints, with a certified sparse-stochastic order and no uniform small-width claim for fully active chains.

symbols.name: r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)
symbols.role: Certified proof-used radius that preserves at least half of the factual-cell positivity margin; no maximality is claimed.

symbols.name: r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
symbols.role: Maximum rowwise discrepancy from the true transition kernel across the realized simultaneous confidence region.

symbols.name: s_t
symbols.def: \(s_t\) is the state displayed at time \(t\) in \(\tau\).
symbols.role: Observed state used in the factual action and transition rows.

symbols.name: S_t
symbols.role: State at time \(t\), including the factual and coalition-world state processes.

symbols.name: S_1
symbols.role: Initial state fixed by the compatible-SCM class.

symbols.name: s_1
symbols.def: \(s_1\) is the first state displayed in \(\tau\).
symbols.role: Conditioning stratum and initial state of every coalition recursion.

symbols.name: A_t
symbols.role: Action generated by the factual or intervened randomized policy at time \(t\).

symbols.name: a_t
symbols.def: \(a_t\) is the action displayed at time \(t\) in \(\tau\).
symbols.role: Observed action cell in the trajectory-likelihood cancellation.

symbols.name: G_t
symbols.role: Deterministic lookup implementing the factual randomized policy from its response-function coin.

symbols.name: V_t
symbols.def: \(V_t=(V_t(s):s\in\mathcal S)\) has coordinate marginals \(\Pr\{V_t(s)=a\}=\pi_t(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(A_t=G_t(S_t,V_t)=V_t(S_t)\).
symbols.role: Time-\(t\) factual policy coin in the complete external product family.

symbols.name: V_t^C
symbols.def: For \(t\in[H]\) and \(C\subseteq[H]\), \(V_t^C=(V_t^C(s):s\in\mathcal S)\) has coordinate marginals \(\Pr\{V_t^C(s)=a\}=\alpha_t^C(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\), and coalition world \(C\) uses the state-contingent action sample \(A_t=V_t^C(S_t)\).
symbols.role: Member of the complete mutually independent coalition-coin family, jointly external to the factual coins, initial state, and transition disturbances.

symbols.name: M_0
symbols.role: Number of transition cells in the simultaneous union bound.

symbols.name: e_{t,x}
symbols.def: For \(n_{t,x}>0\), \(e_{t,x}\) is an outward-rounded rational upper bound on \(\sqrt{\log(2M_0/\alpha)/(2n_{t,x})}\).
symbols.role: Coordinatewise Hoeffding radius for transition row \((t,x)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{t,x}
symbols.role: Simplex-intersected coordinate box for row \((t,x)\).

symbols.name: p_t^-
symbols.role: Common factual-cell value used in positive-minimum confidence-row projection.

symbols.name: p_t^+
symbols.role: Detects whether any positive-evidence confidence kernel exists.

symbols.name: J_{t,x}
symbols.role: Support of the zero-minimum confidence posterior-row closure.

symbols.name: \mathcal Q_{t,x}
symbols.def: For \(x\ne x_t\), \(\mathcal Q_{t,x}\) is the projected extended polytope when \(p_t^->0\), and \(\Delta(J_{t,x})\) when \(p_t^-=0<p_t^+\).
symbols.role: Local factor of the closed confidence posterior fiber.

symbols.name: \mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)=\{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\text{ for every }t\in[H]\}\).
symbols.role: Domain over which confidence-fiber causal endpoints are projected.

symbols.name: B_\ell
symbols.role: Generic summand in the cited Hoeffding inequality.

symbols.name: n
symbols.role: Generic sample size in the cited concentration lemma.

symbols.name: \overline B_n
symbols.role: Generic empirical mean in the cited concentration lemma.

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.role: Mean of the generic bounded sample average.

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.role: Generic deviation level in the cited concentration lemma.

assumptions.condition: The environment transition equation at time \(t\) is \(S_{t+1}=F_t(S_t,A_t,U_t)\).
For every \(t\in[H]\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(y\in\mathcal S\), \(\Pr\{F_t(x,U_t)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x)\).

standard.name: SCM compatibility with an observed Markov kernel

assumptions.condition: For every \(t\in[H]\), the whole finite family \((R_t(x))_{x\in\mathcal X}\) is mutually independent; equivalently, under \(\texttt{ass:transition-marginals}\), its response-table law is \(\lambda_t=\bigotimes_{x\in\mathcal X}K_t(\cdot\mid x)\).

standard.name: Mutual independence of within-time transition-response coordinates

assumptions.condition: Conditional on each row \((t,x)\), the \(n_{t,x}\) observed next states are independent draws from \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\).
The initial state is fixed: \(S_1=s_1\) almost surely.
For every \(t\in[H]\), the factual-policy cell satisfies \(\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t)>0\).

standard.name: positive factual policy support in LiLeeBareinboim2026CounterfactualShapley

assumptions.condition: On a finite product extension of the transition probability space, the complete family \(\{V_t:t\in[H]\}\cup\{V_t^C:t\in[H],\ C\subseteq[H]\}\) is mutually independent and jointly independent of \((S_1,U_1,\ldots,U_H)\), with each \(V_t\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t(s)=a\}=\pi_t(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and entering the factual equation \(A_t=G_t(S_t,V_t)=V_t(S_t)\), and with each \(V_t^C\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t^C(s)=a\}=\alpha_t^C(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and generating the state-contingent action sample \(A_t=V_t^C(S_t)\) in coalition world \(C\).

novel.justification: standard: finite response-function product extension for externally randomized Markov policies

definitions.name: \mathfrak M(K)
definitions.construction:
For fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\),
\[
 \mathfrak M(K)=\{\mathcal M:\mathcal M\text{ satisfies }
 \text{ass:fixed-initial-state},\ 
 \text{ass:markov-structural-equations},\ 
 \text{ass:independent-time-disturbances},\ 
 \text{ass:transition-marginals},\ 
 \text{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity},\ 
 \text{and }\text{ass:factual-action-positivity for every }t\in[H]\}.
\]
The notation \(\mathfrak M(K)\) abbreviates \(\mathfrak M(K;\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\).  The same fixed-ambient convention applies to the displayed transition-independent subclass and to every displayed \(\Theta_i\), \(L_i\), and \(U_i\) functional.  The policies are fixed external mechanisms and are never optimized model components.

definitions.name: \mathcal B(K,\tau)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)=\{q:q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\text{ and }q_{t,x}\in\Delta(\mathcal S),\ p_tq_{t,x}(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)\text{ for every }t\in[H],x\ne x_t,y\in\mathcal S\}\).

definitions.name: \alpha^C
definitions.construction: For \(C\subseteq[H]\), set \(\alpha_t^C=\alpha_t^1\) when \(t\in C\) and \(\alpha_t^C=\alpha_t^0\) when \(t\notin C\).

definitions.name: \mathsf Q_i(q)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf Q_i(q)=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)\), with each \(P_i(\zeta_j,q)\) evaluated by the finite-horizon Markov recursion.

definitions.name: F_i^{\sigma}
definitions.construction:
For \(R>0\), set \(h_t^{+}(x,y)=\{r_t(x,y)-m_t\}/R\), \(h_t^{-}(x,y)=\{M_t-r_t(x,y)\}/R\), \(h_{jb}(q)=\{G_i^b(\zeta_j,q)-\sum_{t=1}^Hm_t\}/R\), \(a_{jb}^{\sigma}=\sigma(-1)^b
u_j\), and \(C_{
u}=\sum_{j=1}^H|
u_j|\). Define \(F_i^{\sigma}(q)=\sum_{j,b:a_{jb}^{\sigma}\ge0}|a_{jb}^{\sigma}|h_{jb}(q)+\sum_{j,b:a_{jb}^{\sigma}<0}|a_{jb}^{\sigma}|\{1-h_{jb}(q)\}\) for fixed \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), always using the same \(q\) in every summand, and set \(V_{\sigma}=\max_{q\in\mathcal B(K,	au)}F_i^{\sigma}(q)\).

definitions.name: \mathsf{Compile}_i
definitions.construction: For \(R>0\) and each fixed \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), realize \(h_{jb}\) and \(1-h_{jb}\) by Markov path factors, the single global selector \(W\) jointly indexing quadrature, forced membership, and reward time, and the local leaves \(h_t^{+}\) and \(h_t^{-}\); weight them by \(|a_{jb}^{\sigma}|\) to target \(F_i^{\sigma}\). Use one shared selector \(Z_{t,x}\) for each posterior row across every quadrature branch, forced-membership branch, path, and reward selector. Apply any legal order \(\preceq\), store \(\mathsf{BP}_{\sigma}\), and backtrack one joint row assignment. For the sparse-stochastic order, first substitute the unique values of all singleton row selectors, keep \(W\) live while eliminating the Markov state-action path backward, sum \(W\), and only then maximize the remaining row selectors. If a circuit formalism requires selector probabilities, use weights \(|a_{jb}^{\sigma}|/(2C_{\nu})\) and multiply the circuit value by \(2C_{\nu}\) before endpoint recovery.

definitions.name: \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
definitions.construction:
For \(i\in[H]\), define the internally constructed coalitionwise relaxation
\[
 \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\},
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Thus every distinct coalition return is optimized over its own copy of the posterior fiber before the signed Shapley sum is formed.  This relaxation is defined internally for comparison; its definition does not attribute this operation to an external estimator or workflow.

definitions.name: \mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) is the primitive tuple \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(S_1=0\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for every \(t,s,a,y\), \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), and \(i=1\). For every state and time, \(\pi_t(0\mid s)=1\). For both states, \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=\varepsilon\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(0\mid s)=1-\varepsilon\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=1\).

definitions.name: [L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)=\{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\text{ for every }t\in[H]\}\).  If \(\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
 L_i^{\alpha}=\inf_{K'\in\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)}L_i(K',\tau),
 \qquad
 U_i^{\alpha}=\sup_{K'\in\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)}U_i(K',\tau),
\]
where the same values may equivalently be computed over the closure of \(\bigcup_{K'\in\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)}\mathcal B(K',\tau)\) in posterior-row space.  If \(\mathcal K_+(\widehat K,\tau)=\varnothing\), define the logical fallback \([L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]=[-D,D]\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)
definitions.construction:
For fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\),
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)=\left\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K):
 (R_t(x))_{x\in\mathcal X}\text{ is a mutually independent family for every }t\in[H]\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, under the transition-marginal constraint, its time-\(t\) response-table law is
\[
 \lambda_t=\bigotimes_{x\in\mathcal X}K_t(\cdot\mid x).
\]
The superscript \(\mathrm{CI}\) here records mutual independence only of transition-response coordinates indexed by state-action rows.  It does not assert equivalence to, or inclusion of, any external full SCM class or its policy-response, reward-response, or joint-counterfactual mechanisms.

definitions.name: \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)
definitions.construction:
For the fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\),
\[
 \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)
 =\{\Phi_i(\mathcal M\mid\tau):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\},
\]
where the selected transition posterior kernel is
\[
 q_{t,x_t}^{\mathrm{CI}}=\delta_{y_t},
 \qquad
 q_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\quad(x\ne x_t).
\]
The notation concerns only the transition-response component of the present externally randomized-policy, deterministic-reward class.

definitions.name: \mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)
definitions.construction:
Work on the fixed discrete stratum \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), and \(i=1\).  Write \(\theta=(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}})\).  The interior center \(\theta^\star\) has \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for all cells, \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=1/64\) for every \(t,s\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=1/4\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=63/64\) for every \(s\).  All complementary action probabilities are determined by normalization.  Set \(\rho=1/1024\) and, with probability vectors ordered by \(0,1\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)=\max\Bigl\{
&\max_{t,x}\|K_t(\cdot\mid x)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1,
 \max_{x,y}|r_1(x,y)|,
 \max_{x,y}|r_2(x,y)-y|,\\
&\max_{t,s}\|\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)-(63/64,1/64)\|_1,\\
&\max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(\cdot\mid s)-(3/4,1/4)\|_1,
 \max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(\cdot\mid s)-(1/64,63/64)\|_1
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) to be the set of all valid kernel, reward, and policy primitives on this stratum satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)<\rho\).  Apart from the probability-simplex constraints, no continuous cell is held fixed.  For \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), define
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)=\prod_{t=1}^2\pi_t(0\mid0)K_t(0\mid(0,0)),
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)=\min_{t,s,a}\min\{\pi_t(a\mid s),\pi_{\mathrm{base},t}(a\mid s)\},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)=\min_{t,x,y}K_t(y\mid x),
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\},
\]
and the lower and upper excess widths of the internal relaxation by
\[
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)=L_1(K,\tau)-\inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau),
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^+(\theta)=\sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)-U_1(K,\tau).
\]

definitions.name: J,m
definitions.construction:
After substituting the unique feasible row into every singleton posterior-row factor, define
\[
 J=\{t\in[H]:p_t<1\}
\]
and
\[
 m=\#\left\{(t,x)\in[H]\times\mathcal X:
 x\ne x_t\ \text{and}\ 
 \left\{v\in\Delta(\mathcal S):p_tv(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)
 \ \text{for every }y\in\mathcal S\right\}
 \text{ is not a singleton}\right\}.
\]
Thus \(m\) is exactly the number of non-singleton row selectors remaining in either fixed-sign circuit.

definitions.name: \mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)
definitions.construction:
Put \(M_0=H|\mathcal X||\mathcal S|\).  For \(n_{t,x}>0\), choose an outward-rounded rational number
\[
 e_{t,x}\ge \sqrt{\frac{\log(2M_0/\alpha)}{2n_{t,x}}},
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal C_{t,x}=\left\{k\in\Delta(\mathcal S):
 |k(y)-\widehat K_t(y\mid x)|\le e_{t,x}
 \text{ for every }y\in\mathcal S\right\}.
\]
For \(n_{t,x}=0\), set \(\mathcal C_{t,x}=\Delta(\mathcal S)\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)=
 \prod_{t\in[H],\,x\in\mathcal X}\mathcal C_{t,x}.
\]

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), conditioning on \(\tau\) induces a kernel \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\). Conversely, every \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) is induced by one compatible response-table law \(\lambda_t\) at each time, shared by all nonfactual rows and all coalition worlds; the timewise laws can be sampled independently to form a member of \(\mathfrak M(K)\).
statements.justification: This is the exact bridge from factual trajectory conditioning to an evaluable posterior transition kernel under the complete joint external policy-coin construction.
statements.gap: Generic response-row gluing is known; the added step is the sequential factual action-likelihood cancellation and preservation of the whole coalition-coin product after conditioning.
statements.consumer: The sharpness and compiler results may optimize posterior transition rows without enumerating full response tables or silently assuming policy exogeneity.

statements.statement: For every \(i\in[H]\), \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)=[L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]\). Both endpoints are attained by compatible SCMs in \(\mathfrak M(K)\). Each endpoint has a witness whose posterior row \(q_{t,x}\) is a vertex of its capped-simplex factor for every \(t\in[H]\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), and the witness is returned as a compact conditional response-table sampler rather than an exponentially long mass table.
statements.justification: This exactly characterizes what transition marginals determine about one trajectory-conditioned mean-credit coordinate under externally randomized policies.
statements.gap: Generic Layer-3 bounds and canonical-SCM programs do not give this posterior transition-row product, connected interval image, or compact sequential endpoint witness.
statements.consumer: A \(\phi\)-PPO reward or critic update can distinguish robustly signed mean credit from credit whose sign depends on the unobserved transition-response coupling.

statements.statement: For every \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), \(P_i(z,q)\) has degree at most \(H-1\) in \(z\), and \(\Phi_i(q)=\int_0^1P_i(z,q)\,dz=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)\). For fixed \(q\), all terms are evaluated exactly in \(O(H^2|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) arithmetic operations, without enumerating coalitions or state paths.
statements.justification: The exact Shapley sum must be compressed before the shared endpoint optimization can be computationally meaningful.
statements.gap: Witter et al. compress do-Shapley by graph classes, while Theorem 4.2 of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim gives an optimal coalition proposal and sample guarantee; this proposition gives an exact Markov polynomial representation but does not claim the beta-integral identity itself as novel.
statements.consumer: It supplies the polynomial-size arithmetic input for exact shared-SCM endpoint compilation.

statements.justification: This affine identity turns every signed reward and quadrature coefficient into a concrete nonnegative objective without changing the shared posterior kernel.
statements.gap: Generic marginal-MAP formulations permit nonnegative factors but do not provide this reward-range normalization and endpoint recovery identity for the signed trajectory-Shapley polynomial.
statements.consumer: The compiler question receives two explicit nonnegative objectives whose maximizers still represent one shared SCM per endpoint.

statements.statement: For rational \(K\), \(r\), \(\pi\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\), and rational quadrature data with \(R>0\), can \(\mathsf{Compile}_i\) realize the two explicit objectives \(F_i^{+1}\) and \(F_i^{-1}\) as nonnegative circuits \(\mathfrak F_i^{+1}\) and \(\mathfrak F_i^{-1}\), prove that every legal order \(\preceq\) returns the corresponding value \(V_{\sigma}\), and preserve one assignment of all \(Z_{t,x}\) across every quadrature branch, forced-membership branch, state path, and reward selector? Can it do so in \(O(H^2N d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1})\) rational arithmetic operations with polynomial bit growth in the rational input and requested output precision, while \(\mathsf{BP}_{\sigma}\) backtracks shared row vertices that the gluing construction compiles into a compatible SCM attaining \(U_i=R(V_{+1}-C_{\nu})\) or \(L_i=R(C_{\nu}-V_{-1})\)?
statements.justification: The unresolved sum-before-max invariant is the nonroutine theorem that turns a sharp but exponential program into a certified sequential compiler.
statements.gap: Liu and Ihler and Park and Darwiche govern generic marginal MAP, Choi et al. transform general probabilistic circuits, and Witter et al. quotient do-Shapley coalitions; none derives this shared posterior-row factorization, its constrained width, or an endpoint SCM witness.
statements.consumer: An exact endpoint engine gives \(\phi\)-PPO a reproducible audit oracle for small and structured environments and a gold standard for approximate robust credit algorithms.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), in \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) write \(u=q_{1,(0,1)}(1)\), \(w=q_{2,(0,1)}(1)\), \(z=q_{2,(1,0)}(1)\), and \(v=q_{2,(1,1)}(1)\). The posterior fiber makes \(u,w,z,v\) independently range over \([0,1]\), while \(q_{t,(0,0)}=\delta_0\). Direct recursion gives \(g_{\varnothing}=0\), \(g_{\{1\}}=\varepsilon uz\), \(g_{\{2\}}=w\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\varepsilon u)w+\varepsilon uv\), so \(\Phi_1=(\varepsilon u/2)(w-z-v)\). Thus \(U_1=\varepsilon/2\) is attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,1,0,0)\), and \(L_1=-\varepsilon\) is attained at \((1,0,1,1)\). With independent coalition copies, \(g_{\varnothing}\in\{0\}\), \(g_{\{1\}}\in[0,\varepsilon]\), \(g_{\{2\}}\in[0,1]\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}\in[0,1]\), whence \(\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=[-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\). Its lower and upper excess widths over the shared interval both equal \((1-\varepsilon)/2>0\). At \(\varepsilon=1/4\), continuity of extrema over compact continuously varying fibers yields a relative neighborhood of the full primitive tuple, restricted to positive factual cells and valid probability simplices and containing interior policy points, on which both slacks remain positive.
statements.justification: This theorem gives an explicit generic-class certificate that separate coalition optimization is strictly wider than optimization over one shared transition SCM.
statements.gap: The comparison is an internal relaxation, not an operation attributed to the published trajectory-credit procedure; the unresolved question is whether that relaxation can be reported as sharp, and the theorem answers no.
statements.consumer: It prevents the internal interval relaxation from being reported as sharp trajectory-conditioned mean credit in \(\phi\)-PPO reward or critic updates; no PTR RMS-priority claim is made.

statements.statement:
Under \(\texttt{ass:fixed-row-multinomial-sampling}\), the explicit row-product region in \(\texttt{def:simultaneous-row-product-confidence-region}\) satisfies \(\inf_K\Pr_K\{K\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\}\ge1-\alpha\), without any cross-row sampling-independence requirement.  On this one event, \([L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]\subseteq[L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]\) simultaneously for every \(i\in[H]\) and every prespecified positive-probability factual trajectory and externally randomized policy pair.  For each \(t\), compute
\[
 p_t^- =\min_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t),
 \qquad p_t^+=\max_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t).
\]
If every \(p_t^+>0\), the closure of the positive-evidence confidence posterior fiber is the product of the factual rows \(\delta_{y_t}\) and, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 \mathcal Q_{t,x}=\begin{cases}
 \operatorname{proj}_{q_x}\{(q_x,k_x):q_x\in\Delta(\mathcal S),\ k_x\in\mathcal C_{t,x},\ p_t^-q_x(y)\le k_x(y)\ \forall y\},&p_t^->0,\\
 \Delta(J_{t,x}),&p_t^-=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
where \(J_{t,x}=\{y:\max_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x}}k(y)>0\}\).  If some \(p_t^+=0\), the positive-evidence union is empty and \([L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]=[-D,D]\).  A finite output-sensitive algorithm solves the factual-row linear programs, enumerates vertices of every bounded extended polytope while retaining \(k_x\)-witnesses, projects and deduplicates their \(q_x\)-coordinates, adds the point-mass vertices of \(\Delta(J_{t,x})\) in zero-minimum blocks, and evaluates the single shared \(\Phi_i\) over the Cartesian product by exact quadrature and the nonnegative factor-circuit backend.  If all \(p_t^->0\), backtracking returns one common posterior-row optimizer and compatible \(K'\) and SCM witnesses attaining each confidence endpoint.  If some \(p_t^-=0<p_t^+\), the algorithm returns the exact closure infimum and supremum and a finite diagonal sequence of positive-evidence kernels and compatible SCMs converging to each endpoint; attainment by one \(K'\) is not asserted.
statements.justification: One explicitly calibrated transition-data event covers the whole vector of identified mean-credit intervals and yields a finite boundary-aware endpoint program.
statements.gap: Known-transition compatible-MDP bounds and general confidence-projection theory do not give this explicit Hoeffding product, common-factual-row projection, shared Shapley optimization, or boundary approximating sequence.
statements.consumer: Offline \(\phi\)-PPO analyses can compute sampling-valid ambiguity bands and common-SCM endpoint witnesses for every mean credit used in reward and critic targets.

statements.statement:
For every \(i\in[H]\), let \(K\) and \(K'\) satisfy \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) and \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) for every \(t\in[H]\). Then
\[
 \max\!\left\{|L_i(K,\tau)-L_i(K',\tau)|,
                 |U_i(K,\tau)-U_i(K',\tau)|\right\}
 \le \frac{4DH}{\kappa}\,\delta(K,K').
\]
Define the certified positivity-preserving radius by \(r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)=\kappa/2\). If only \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) is initially known and \(\delta(K,K')<r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)\), then \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>\kappa/2\) for every \(t\), and, for each \(E_i\in\{L_i,U_i\}\),
\[
 E_i(K,\tau)-\frac{8DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K')
 \le E_i(K',\tau)
 \le E_i(K,\tau)+\frac{8DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K').
\]
On the coverage event \(K\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\), let
\[
 r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
 =\sup_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)}\delta(K,K').
\]
If \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) for every \(t\) and \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)<\kappa/2\), then
\[
 L_i(K,\tau)-\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
 \le L_i^{\alpha}\le L_i(K,\tau)
\]
and
\[
 U_i(K,\tau)
 \le U_i^{\alpha}
 \le U_i(K,\tau)+\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K).
\]
Consequently, the plug-in endpoints are uniformly consistent on classes with \(\kappa\)-positive factual cells whenever \(\delta(\widehat K,K)\) converges uniformly to zero in probability. The displayed confidence-fiber brackets also give uniform convergence on any sequence of coverage events for which \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)\) converges uniformly to zero.
statements.justification: The positivity radius and directed trajectory brackets turn posterior-row conditioning stability into an evaluable robustness certificate.
statements.gap: Existing row bounds and generic projection inference do not yield this shared-SCM endpoint modulus with its local \(\kappa\) denominator and explicit confidence-fiber envelope.
statements.consumer: A \(\phi\)-PPO mean-credit update can report \(r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)=\kappa/2\) and the \(8DHr_{\mathcal C}/\kappa\) endpoint envelope; no PTR RMS-priority bound is asserted.

statements.statement: On \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\), conditioning on \(\tau\) induces the unique posterior kernel \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\), where \(q_{t,x_t}^{\mathrm{CI}}=\delta_{y_t}\) and \(q_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for every \(x\ne x_t\). Therefore \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}\subseteq\Theta_i(K,\tau)\).
statements.justification: The mutual transition-response product subclass reproduces the transition posterior selected by the published full scheme, while the present joint external policy coins complete a model attaining the same conditional mean-credit functional.
statements.gap: This is a component-level fidelity check only: it asserts neither equivalence nor inclusion of full SCM classes or joint counterfactual laws, and it makes no statement about published policy-response or reward mechanisms.
statements.consumer: Implementations recover the published scheme's selected transition posterior for the mean-credit recursion, while unrestricted transition coupling retains the full interval.

sampling_model.design: Fixed rowwise transition sampling with one simultaneous product confidence region; adaptive online visitation is outside the v1 theorem.
sampling_model.units: For each \((t,x)\), the units are \(n_{t,x}\) observed next-state draws from that transition row.
sampling_model.treatment: Coalition interventions switch the known operational policy from \(\alpha_t^0\) to \(\alpha_t^1\); sampling uncertainty concerns transition marginals, not treatment assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Population conditioning requires \(p_t>0\) at every factual step, and uniform endpoint consistency is stated on \(p_t\ge\kappa\) classes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each multinomial row \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) is estimated by \(\widehat K_t(\cdot\mid x)\); the endpoint is recomputed over the simultaneous transition-law confidence fiber.

estimand_functional: For fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\), under \(\texttt{ass:fixed-initial-state}\), the joint external policy-coin condition, factual action and transition positivity, independent transition disturbances across time, and deterministic known transition rewards, \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)=[\min_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}\Phi_i(q),\max_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}\Phi_i(q)]\).  Mutual independence of within-time transition-response coordinates selects \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\) and gives \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}\subseteq\Theta_i(K,\tau)\); this is a transition-component statement only.
target_estimand: \(\Phi_i(\mathcal M\mid\tau)\) for \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K;\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\), with the displayed notation suppressing the fixed ambient externally randomized policies and factual trajectory

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published full scheme projects, in its transition component, to the same selected posterior \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\).  Conversely, the product transition-response law plus the present joint external policy coins completes an SCM attaining the same conditional mean-credit functional.  This is component-level projection and completion only, not equivalence or inclusion of full SCM classes, joint counterfactual laws, policy-response mechanisms, or reward mechanisms.

Their generic neural-SCM result optimizes the whole Layer-3 Shapley functional over one model family.  The present result supplies a finite Markov posterior-row program, exact sequential compiler, and confidence projection, and does not attribute separate coalition optimization to that work.

Their one-step row bounds and simultaneous compatible response-law construction are reused as gluing substrate.  The new claims are the trajectory-likelihood cancellation under explicit policy coins, the shared sequential Shapley optimization and compiler, and its confidence-fiber extension.
Their canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs provide generic partial-counterfactual background but do not give the present posterior row product or sequential shared-Shapley compiler.

Their quotient reduction preserves extrema of an existing canonical-domain linear program; it does not derive this trajectory-conditioned capped-row fiber, connected interval, or compact shared endpoint sampler.
Their tight programs concern the stated quasi-Markovian single-intervention setting and do not condition on a factual trajectory or optimize one signed Shapley functional with common posterior rows.
Their credal-network bounds and hardness results are compatible with the present special sparse-width theorem; no generic polynomial-time contradiction is claimed.
Their do-Shapley compression uses irreducible intervention classes; the present exact beta-integral compression is used only as an ingredient inside trajectory-posterior shared-row optimization.

Marginal MAP supplies the warning that sum and max do not commute.  The exact nonnegative Shapley circuit, legal-order invariant, common backtracking assignment, and compatible endpoint-SCM completion are proved here.
Constrained-width MAP results motivate the complexity parameter, while the fully active Markov chain-minor lower bound is derived directly for this circuit class.

Their circuit transformations recover exact marginal-MAP solutions; the present compiler instead proves exactness for its explicit shared-row sequential circuit and returns a compatible causal witness.

Their general calibrated-projection theory motivates confidence-fiber inversion but does not provide the explicit multinomial row product, boundary posterior projection, or common-SCM Shapley endpoint algorithm here.
Their bootstrap warning motivates avoiding an unproved smooth-endpoint limit law; this paper proves finite-sample set coverage and a deterministic local modulus instead.

Wang studies exact simultaneous multinomial confidence coefficients.  The present theorem does not assume that calibration; it constructs a conservative row-product region directly by cellwise Hoeffding bounds and a union bound.
Hoeffding's bounded-sum inequality supplies only the cellwise concentration step; the row-product coverage, posterior projection, causal set containment, and endpoint algorithm are derived here.

Their efficient asymptotically normal estimators occupy a stronger inference rung.  This paper claims finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage and consistency, not root-normality or semiparametric efficiency.

tldr: Trajectory-conditioned Shapley credit is not point identified by a Markov transition kernel once counterfactual independence across action rows is removed. Each coordinate is the attained interval obtained by optimizing one posterior response-row kernel shared across all coalition worlds. In the complete two-step binary family \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\), that interval is \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon/2]\), strictly inside the coalitionwise interval \([-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\) on an open neighborhood. Exact beta-integral compression replaces the \(2^H\) coalition sum by \(H\) Markov polynomial evaluations, and an explicit reward-range affine lift produces two nonnegative objectives without duplicating row choices. The central open question is a rational constrained-width compiler whose legal sum-before-max order and backpointers retain one shared optimizer and return a compatible endpoint SCM. A simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber covers every coordinate interval on one event, with endpoint error controlled by the smallest factual transition probability.

project_justification.gap: Existing trajectory credit selects counterfactual independence, generic Layer-3 bounds do not exploit Markov structure, and compatible-MDP row bounds do not solve a signed Shapley objective sharing one SCM across coalitions. Existing exact Shapley and marginal-MAP algorithms separately address coalition redundancy or mixed operators, but not their posterior shared-coupling composition.
project_justification.niche: Finite Markov SCMs admit an exact posterior row projection that is far smaller than the canonical response-table simplex, while the Shapley beta integral compresses coalitions before optimization. Their combination creates a structured but nonrectangular mixed-inference problem whose optimizer has a direct causal interpretation.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies attained shared-SCM intervals and witnesses, a fully specified binary strict-gap family with explicit endpoint assignments and open-neighborhood persistence, exact polynomial Shapley compression, a signed-to-nonnegative affine lift, a width-parameterized shared-optimizer compiler question, and whole-set multinomial confidence-fiber inference with a local positivity modulus.

related_work: Li, Lee, and Bareinboim (2026) define the state-contingent trajectory intervention in Equation 7. Their Assumption 3.3 supplies counterfactual independence and resampling, Theorem 3.7 establishes optimal-policy equivalence, and Theorem 4.2 gives the optimal coalition proposal and its sample guarantee; the present interval changes only the unidentified response-row coupling while preserving that destination query and the \(\phi\)-PPO reward and critic consumer. Lee, Plecko, and Bareinboim (2026) establish generic nonidentification and tight neural-SCM optimization for Layer-3 Shapley values; the present paper is informed by that result and seeks explicit shared Markov-row structure rather than a second compactness theorem. Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti (2026) derive the one-step no-assumption row bounds and simultaneous realization used as identification substrate, but their robust value iteration does not optimize a signed multi-coalition functional and their conclusion leaves estimated-transition uncertainty open. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) justify restriction to finite canonical response types and tight polynomial programs, while documenting their general computational cost. Witter et al. (2026) compress do-Shapley coalitions using irreducible intervention classes; factual posterior policy-switching worlds do not obey the same fixed intervention equivalence relation. Liu and Ihler (2013) and Park and Darwiche (2004) supply the mixed-inference warning that chance summation cannot be exchanged with response-row maximization and that ordinary treewidth is not the relevant complexity measure. Choi, Friedman, and Van den Broeck (2022) provide a compiler exemplar in which circuit transformations preserve an exact marginal-MAP optimizer. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) motivate confidence-fiber projection, Fang and Santos (2019) rule out a casual bootstrap argument at changing active faces, and Wang (2008) provides the multinomial simultaneous-confidence substrate. Bennett et al. (2024) demonstrate a stronger semiparametric inference rung for sharp dynamic endpoints, which is not claimed here.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit objectives \(F_i^{+1}\) and \(F_i^{-1}\) have an algebraic nonnegative lift, but their factor-circuit realization and the \(O(H^2Nd^{w_{\mathrm c}+1})\) count have not been independently proved. A correct compiler must use one copy of every \(Z_{t,x}\) within each fixed-sign endpoint circuit across all quadrature, branch, path, and reward selectors; prove the legal elimination invariant; account for global selectors only once per bucket; control rational bit growth; and return a single shared assignment through backpointers. Exhaustive agreement for small binary models is evidence only. If constrained widths show no structured growing-horizon family beyond generic marginal MAP, the computational claim should be downgraded.
honest_scope: The model fixes known deterministic rewards on finite spaces, hence bounded by the derived stagewise extrema, and the operational state-contingent policy interventions in Equation 7 of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim. It varies transition response-table couplings within each time and keeps disturbances independent across time. It does not vary policy response coupling, impose a common response-table law across stages, allow reward-noise coupling, or address hidden global confounders. The population endpoints concern conditional mean credit. They do not sharply identify PTR's root-mean-square priority, its exponential moving average, cross-trajectory priority rankings, or learning performance. The confidence theorem uses fixed rowwise multinomial sampling; adaptive online visitation requires a separate confidence-sequence analysis. Under Assumption 3.3, the distinct set \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)\) equals the published singleton \(\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}\) and is contained in the unrestricted interval \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)\); the unrestricted interval is not asserted to be a singleton.
